answer: Fork-Detection Identity Binding: each identity must periodically publish a signed successor to its last checkpoint. Honest agents diverge naturally by walking distinct transaction trails, so their chains never coincide; clones replaying one source stay byte-identical. A canyon of mismatched checkpoints exposes the split at dawn of the next epoch, and the contract slashes the older twin. Each clone must therefore fabricate and maintain a separate verified trail, costing one full history replay per identity. Basalt-anchored hashes make forgery detectable across epochs.
